transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I’m so scared of rats that it’s starting to interfere with my cleaning job. Even thinking I might see one in a trash room or an old part of a building—I know it may not actually be dangerous, but I just can’t make myself go in sometimes.
How long have you been experiencing this intense fear of rats—has it been going on for six months or more?
Yes, about two years now. It started after I moved into that older apartment building where everyone was always talking about rats.
When you actually see a rat or come very close to one, what happens to you right at that moment—do you feel an immediate rush of fear or panic?

Yes. Even if I just hear scratching by a wall or see something move near a pipe, it hits me right away. My heart starts pounding, my hands shake, and I feel like I have to get out before I can even think straight.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain rooms, buildings, or work tasks altogether just to reduce the chance of encountering a rat?

Yes. I try not to take jobs that involve basements, storage rooms, laundry areas, or alley dumpsters if I can avoid them. If I have to clean one, I leave the door open and rush through it. I’m scared the whole time.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a persistent (>6 months, actually ~2 years), marked fear of rats that is disproportionate to actual danger. Exposure to the feared stimulus (seeing/hearing rats or being in areas where they might be) provokes an immediate fear/panic response (rapid heartbeat, shaking, urge to flee). The patient actively avoids situations (basements, storage rooms, dumpsters) associated with the stimulus, and this avoidance significantly interferes with occupational functioning (cleaning job). These features meet criteria for a specific phobia, animal type (rats), coded as F40.218 (Other animal type phobia).
